hook: Mark Chen has been at OpenAI since 2018, moving from quantitative trading into leading some of the company's most visible research programs. He co-led the team that built DALL-E, directed the vision work that gave GPT-4 its multimodal capabilities, and oversaw Codex, the model behind GitHub Copilot. In March 2025 OpenAI named him Chief Research Officer, a role focused on integrating research and product development so new capabilities move into deployment faster. He also coaches the USA Computing Olympiad team, a pastime that tracks with his own path through competitive mathematics and computer science at MIT.

standing.watch: The records show no pending case naming Chen personally, so the open items are the OpenAI matters tracked on the site. Each of those cases is marked as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker, including TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Bass v. The records give no dates for most of these beyond the filing markers, and no outcome, so what comes next is simply further docket activity. Nothing in the records indicates a planned listing, a named dispute involving Chen, or any other scheduled event for him. Where the records are thin, they stay thin.
standing.record: The site's records place Chen at one company, OpenAI, where he is listed as an executive. His background runs through MIT, where he earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics with computer science in 2012, and through competitive mathematics and computer science, which he continues as a coach of the USA Computing Olympiad team. The lawsuits on the site name OpenAI entities rather than Chen himself, including TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, and Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC. One case, Buist v. Anthropic, PBC, names a different company and does not involve OpenAI. Across these records the pattern is a research leader whose public footprint is the models he built and the executive role he now holds, while the legal activity sits with the company rather than with him.
standing.standing: Mark Chen is Chief Research Officer at OpenAI, a position he has held since March 24, 2025. In that role he is responsible for integrating research and product development so that new capabilities move into deployment faster. The records show he has been at OpenAI since 2018, after working as a quantitative trader at Jane Street Capital building machine-learning models for futures and equities trading. He co-led the team behind DALL-E, directed the vision work that gave GPT-4 image-understanding capability, and led Codex, the model underlying GitHub Copilot. He is credited on OpenAI's GPT-4 contributions page as Vision team co-lead and Deployment lead, and on the o1 contributions page under Leadership and Executive Leadership.
